decisive_items: left breast carcinoma diagnosed eleven years earlier
atypical cells were strongly positive for GATA3
response.rationale: History of breast carcinoma and GATA3-positive atypical cells in dermal vessels are diagnostic of cutaneous metastasis of breast carcinoma; angiosarcoma/Stewart-Treves would require CD31-positive tumor cells and typical lymphedema/limb presentation.

rejected.why: Atypical cells are GATA3-positive, not CD31-positive; CD31 positivity is in vessel lining cells, so angiosarcoma is not supported.

Stewart-Treves syndrome is an angiosarcoma arising in chronic lymphedema, typically on the ipsilateral arm after mastectomy; no lymphedema and facial location with GATA3 positivity favor breast carcinoma metastasis.
